name: ppopf
transitions: real->protected (CR0.PE 0->1, CS far-jump to 32-bit flat code segment 0x08)

delivery_records.real_popf_iopl3: real-mode popfd loads IOPL=3 + IF (EFLAGS 0x...3202); the OLD hardcoded 'user' mask 0x00244DD5 kept IOPL=0 here -> the DOS-Quake divergence
delivery_records.real_popf_iopl0: a second real-mode popfd loads IOPL=0 + IF=0 -> proves IOPL is genuinely writable in real mode (not stuck at 3)
delivery_records.pm_cpl0_popf: PM CPL=0 popfd loads IOPL=2 + IF + ID, with VM held 0 (POPF never loads VM/RF)
delivery_records.success_proof: all three POPF results verified by PUSHF read-back + cmp; exits isa-debug-exit status 133. A core using the always-'user' mask (IOPL/IF held at the old value) DIVERGES per-record from the qemu -cpu pentium golden AND fails the self-check (exit status 67)

description: Bare-metal directed test for the MODE/CPL-aware POPF writable-flag mask (IA-32 SDM Vol.1 POPF). PHASE A (real mode, PE=0): a 32-bit popfd loading IOPL=3 + IF must take BOTH (the architectural real-mode rule); a second popfd loads IOPL=0/IF=0 to prove IOPL is writable, not stuck. PHASE B (protected mode, CPL=0): a popfd loads IOPL=2 + IF + ID while VM stays 0 (POPF never loads VM/RF). Every retired instruction's EFLAGS is captured in the system golden and diffed per-record vs qemu-system-i386 -cpu pentium. This is the DOS-Quake fix's regression guard: the core previously hardcoded the CPL>IOPL 'user' mask 0x00244DD5 for EVERY POPF, so a real-mode popfd (CWSDPMI/go32 at cs=0x2593) kept IOPL=0 where qemu loads IOPL=3, derailing the DPMI register frame. A core with the wrong mask diverges on the very POPFs above and the diff FAILS; with the mode/CPL-aware mask it matches exactly (and the self-check exit code is also a guard: 133 pass / 67 fail). NO paging; the only mode transition is real->protected for PHASE B.
